description: Seed golden set for end-to-end retrieval evaluation. SYNTHETIC: 40 hand-written QA documents, 33 questions in six classes, plus 3,000 deterministic filler documents that reuse the common QA vocabulary to flood naive OR queries. It proves the harness and guards against regressions such as the lexical-search defect; it is NOT a substitute for 100-200 real questions from your own projects with their expected sources, which should be added to this file (or a project-specific one) and tracked over time.

corpus.title: Checkout payment rules
corpus.content: The checkout flow must reject expired credit cards and show a retry message to returning customers. Declined payments are logged with the processor reason code. See TC-0045 for the card decline scenarios.

corpus.title: Refund policy
corpus.content: Refunds are issued within five business days of approval. Partial refunds require a reason code and a manager sign-off. Refund requests older than ninety days need finance approval. Tracked as STORY-12.

corpus.title: Release checklist
corpus.content: A release requires a passing regression suite, an approved sign-off from the product owner and a completed rollback rehearsal. Deployments happen on Tuesday after the code freeze.

corpus.title: Stable regression suites
corpus.content: A stable regression suite avoids shared state, isolates test data per run and retries only infrastructure failures. Quarantine tests that fail intermittently and track them in a flaky list.

corpus.title: Flaky test triage
corpus.content: Flaky tests are triaged weekly. Capture the failure rate over the last twenty runs, the environment and the first failing commit before opening a defect. Example: BUG-77 failed one run in five.

corpus.title: Defect severity levels
corpus.content: Severity one means the product is unusable or data is lost. Severity two blocks a major workflow without a workaround. Severity three has a workaround. Severity four is cosmetic.

corpus.title: Defect lifecycle
corpus.content: A defect moves from new to triaged, in progress, fixed, verified and closed. Reopened defects return to triaged with the verification notes attached.

corpus.title: Test data management
corpus.content: Test data sets are versioned and masked. Never copy production customer records into a test environment. Synthetic accounts are generated by the seed script.

corpus.title: Staging environment
corpus.content: The staging environment mirrors production configuration. It is refreshed nightly and deployments to staging trigger the smoke suite automatically.

corpus.title: Smoke suite
corpus.content: The smoke suite covers login, search and checkout. It must finish in under ten minutes and gates every deployment to staging.

corpus.title: API contract testing
corpus.content: Consumer driven contract tests verify that the payments API still returns the fields that the mobile app reads. A breaking change requires a new API version.

corpus.title: Accessibility checks
corpus.content: Every release is scanned for WCAG 2.1 AA issues. Keyboard navigation and screen reader labels are tested manually for new pages.

corpus.title: Performance budgets
corpus.content: Page load must stay under two seconds at the 95th percentile. The performance test fails the build when the budget is exceeded for two consecutive runs.

corpus.title: Security scanning
corpus.content: Dependency and container scans run on every merge request. Critical vulnerabilities block the release until patched or formally accepted.

corpus.title: Mobile device matrix
corpus.content: Mobile releases are tested on the three most used Android devices and the two latest iOS versions. Device farm sessions are recorded for failed steps.

corpus.title: QA onboarding
corpus.content: New testers get access to the staging environment, the test management tool and the defect tracker in their first week. A buddy walks them through the regression suite.

corpus.title: Sprint ceremonies
corpus.content: Sprint planning sets the scope, the daily standup surfaces blockers, the review demos finished stories and the retrospective picks one improvement to try.

corpus.title: Requirements traceability
corpus.content: Every story links to the test cases that verify its acceptance criteria. Coverage gaps are listed in the weekly quality report.

corpus.title: Writing acceptance criteria
corpus.content: Acceptance criteria are written as Given When Then scenarios. Each criterion must be testable and describe a single observable outcome.

corpus.title: Stable locators
corpus.content: Prefer data test id attributes over CSS paths. Locators that depend on text or layout break when copy changes and cause maintenance work.

corpus.title: CI pipeline stages
corpus.content: The pipeline runs lint, unit tests, build, smoke tests and then deploys to staging. A red pipeline blocks merges to the main branch.

corpus.title: Incident reviews
corpus.content: After a production incident the team writes a blameless review within three business days listing the timeline, contributing factors and follow-up actions.

corpus.title: Search relevance
corpus.content: Product search ranks exact title matches first, then prefix matches, then description matches. Synonyms are configured per locale.

corpus.title: Login throttling
corpus.content: Five failed login attempts lock the account for fifteen minutes. The lock message must not reveal whether the username exists.

corpus.title: Email notifications
corpus.content: Order confirmation emails are sent within one minute. Failed deliveries are retried three times with exponential backoff before an alert is raised.

corpus.title: Idempotency keys
corpus.content: Clients send an idempotency key header with each payment request so a retried request cannot charge a customer twice.

corpus.title: Data migration testing
corpus.content: Migrations are rehearsed on a copy of production data volume. Row counts and checksums are compared before and after the cutover.

corpus.title: Localization testing
corpus.content: Check text expansion, right to left layouts and date formats for every supported locale before release.

corpus.title: Exploratory testing
corpus.content: Exploratory sessions are time boxed to ninety minutes with a charter and notes. Findings are logged as defects with reproduction steps.

corpus.title: Test estimation
corpus.content: Estimate testing effort from the number of acceptance criteria and risky integrations, and reserve a buffer for regression.

corpus.title: Rollback procedure
corpus.content: To roll back, redeploy the previous artifact, restore the database snapshot if a migration ran and announce the rollback in the release channel.

corpus.title: Feature flags
corpus.content: New features ship behind flags. Test both the enabled and disabled paths and remove the flag once the feature is fully released.

corpus.title: Browser support matrix
corpus.content: Support the two latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge. Internet Explorer is no longer supported.

corpus.title: Quality reporting
corpus.content: The weekly quality report lists pass rate, open defects by severity, flaky tests and coverage gaps for each release.

corpus.title: Risk based testing
corpus.content: Prioritize tests by business impact and likelihood of failure. Payment and login flows are always tested first.

corpus.title: Service virtualization
corpus.content: Use mocks for third party services in automated tests and run a nightly job against the real sandbox to catch drift.

corpus.title: Bug bash
corpus.content: Before a major release the whole team spends two hours exploring the product and logs findings in a shared sheet.

corpus.title: Test pyramid
corpus.content: Keep most checks as fast unit tests, fewer integration tests and only a handful of end to end journeys.

corpus.title: Session timeout
corpus.content: Idle sessions expire after thirty minutes. Users see a warning two minutes before the timeout.

corpus.title: Cache invalidation
corpus.content: Product price changes purge the CDN cache within one minute. Test that stale prices are never shown at checkout.
